summary: Ustaz Azlan explains the Prophet's SAW strategy during the three years of the closed call: a strategic individual call that was not secret, the first waves who accepted Islam, the hadith of Amr ibn Abasah in Sahih Muslim, the mentoring circles, and Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas's striking of a polytheist that led the Prophet SAW to teach patience. The ustaz explains why Dar al-Arqam was chosen as headquarters, what was taught there (tawhid, Paradise, Hell, character, the names of Allah), the five lessons that resulted (faith, patience, sincerity, trust, loyal friendship), gradual development, and mentorship as the key to unlocking hidden potential.
keyPoints: The first three years of the call were closed and individual, not secret, and the Prophet SAW judged who was suitable to approach.
After the Prophet's SAW family, Abu Bakr brought five important companions, followed by a second and third wave until about 40 people.
Of the first 40, only about 13 were from the weak; the movement was not a class or tribal clash.
The Prophet SAW did not permit a physical response even though Sa'd struck a polytheist.
Dar al-Arqam was chosen because it lay in Banu Makhzum territory, belonged to a youth and was shielded by hills.
Teaching at Dar al-Arqam stressed the Quran, tawhid, Paradise, Hell and character, producing faith, patience, sincerity, trust and loyal friendship.
Gradual development and mentorship build character and release hidden potential.

lessons.title: Sincerity leads to the truth
lessons.body: Amr ibn Abasah found the Prophet SAW though his location was hidden, thanks to his determination.

lessons.title: Strategic da'wah assesses the recipient
lessons.body: The Prophet SAW chose whom to tell and whom not to, even within the family.

lessons.title: Not a clash of class or tribe
lessons.body: The early followers came from many statuses, tribes and nations.

lessons.title: Be patient when wronged
lessons.body: Even with strength, the companions were not allowed a physical response in the early phase.

lessons.title: Victory will come; do not rush
lessons.body: The Prophet SAW told Khabbab to be patient because Allah's promise is certain.

lessons.title: Empathy for silent believers
lessons.body: Some new Muslims do not register or show their Islam because of family and legal consequences.

lessons.title: Build the foundation of faith before rulings
lessons.body: For 13 years in Makkah the focus was tawhid, Paradise, Hell, character and justice, before rulings in Madinah.

lessons.title: True friendship
lessons.body: The Prophet's SAW companions were loyal without self-interest; today many face a friendship crisis.

lessons.title: Change happens gradually
lessons.body: Gradual process is a universal law from individual to state.

lessons.title: Mentorship releases potential
lessons.body: Mentors who invest in relationships and social capital change lives.

lessons.title: Character matters more than talent
lessons.body: The Prophet SAW built the companions' character and used each one's strengths, like Abu Bakr's.

dalil.context: Shows the closed call was strategic, not secret.
dalil.translation: Amr ibn Abasah came from Yemen looking for the Prophet SAW, who said he was sent to join family ties, break idols and affirm Allah's oneness, with a free man and a slave beside him, and told him to go home and come when he had power.

dalil.context: How the Prophet SAW trained the early generation to be patient.
dalil.translation: The Prophet SAW told Khabbab that earlier peoples had their heads sawn and their flesh combed from the bone; Allah will complete this matter, but you are in a hurry.

dalil.context: The basis of releasing people's hidden potential.
dalil.translation: People are like mines; the best of them in jahiliyyah are the best in Islam if they understand religion.

dalil.context: An example of Umar's transformation once he embraced Islam.
dalil.translation: If Umar takes one road Satan takes another; and if there were a prophet after me, it would be Umar.

dalil.context: The story of a companion who wished to sell wine after its prohibition in Madinah.
dalil.translation: What is forbidden, its sale price is also forbidden.

dalil.context: Friendship as an extension of keeping family ties.
dalil.translation: Whoever wants his life lengthened and blessed should keep family ties.
